THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Protein Mashed Popcorn

Buttery mashed potatoes without a stick of butter: 700g peeled gold potatoes mashed with blended Good Culture 2% cottage cheese, Nurri whole protein milk, and 1 tbsp Kernel Season’s Butter Popcorn Seasoning. Makes 4 servings at ≈180 calories, 9g protein, and 1.6g fat each.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME20 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~180 cal | ~9g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Weigh the 700g gold potatoes after peeling so the 4-portion nutrition calculation stays exact, and save the peels to air-fry into Crispy Potato Skins.

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 700g gold potatoes, peeled and weighed raw (save the peels for Crispy Potato Skins)
  • 150g Good Culture 2% cottage cheese
  • 1/4 cup Nurri whole ultra-filtered protein milk
  • 1 tbsp Kernel Season’s Butter Popcorn Seasoning

Allergens: dairy.

You want real-potato mash with unmistakable buttery flavor for ~180 calories, 9g protein, and 1.6g fat per serving instead of loading the bowl with 4 tablespoons of butter.

Method

  1. 1.BOIL & MASH POTATOES. Peel 700g raw gold potatoes (save the peels for Crispy Potato Skins) and boil in water until fork-tender. Drain and mash or rice while hot.
  2. 2.BLEND COTTAGE CHEESE & PROTEIN MILK. Blend 150g Good Culture 2% cottage cheese and 1/4 cup Nurri whole protein milk until completely smooth, then pour over the hot mashed potatoes.
  3. 3.ADD BUTTER POPCORN SEASONING. Sprinkle in 1 tbsp Kernel Season’s Butter Popcorn Seasoning.
  4. 4.FOLD & SERVE (4 PORTIONS). Fold until smooth and creamy, then divide into 4 equal servings.

Keys to success

  • Blend the cottage cheese and Nurri milk completely smooth before folding into the hot potatoes so there are zero curds.
  • Kernel Season’s Butter Popcorn Seasoning contains real butter powder and salt, delivering butter flavor and seasoning in one step.

Storage and reheating

Store: Store leftover mash in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days.

Reheat: Warm gently on the stovetop or in the microwave with a splash of milk to loosen.

Lasts: 3–4 days refrigerated.
